things.name: the old house
things.who: the Greys' house from the first record of a 'capital messuage' in the 1280s, altered many times (a classical north front about 1671–1676, refaced fronts in 1791), until it was pulled down from 1834

things.name: the old house's classical north front
things.who: added for Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, and his wife Mary, paid for largely from her inheritance of 1671, with Amabel keeping the accounts (the listing says 1671; Bedfordshire Archives 1672; the History of Parliament 1672 to 1676)

things.name: the old house's demolition
things.who: carried out by Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, while his new house was built; watercolours show parts still standing in 1838

things.name: Thomas Carew's poem 'To my friend G.N. from Wrest'
things.who: written by Thomas Carew while a guest of Henry, 8th Earl of Kent, and his wife Elizabeth Talbot, in spring 1639

things.name: the round fountain and its eight statues
things.who: acquired for Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, after she inherited in 1859, according to its listing; Bedfordshire Archives says about 1840 for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey. The statues round it are early to mid nineteenth century on pedestals of the early 1700s

things.name: the sundial
things.who: made by Henry Wynne, a London instrument maker, as his plate signed and dated 1682 shows; the plate in the garden today is a replica

things.name: the six marble statues round the sundial
things.who: probably bought for Thomas, 2nd Earl de Grey, about 1840 (Bedfordshire Archives), or by his daughter Anne Florence, Countess Cowper, after 1859 (Historic England, which mentions the 1862 Exhibition)

things.name: the Long Water
things.who: made for Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, and his wife Mary, with his mother Amabel; extended and given its Pavilion by Henry, Duke of Kent, in the early 1700s. The exact date is uncertain: early 1680s (English Heritage) or before 1685 (a 2013 survey)

things.name: the statue of Mercury and Cupid
things.who: probably of the late 1600s, perhaps by Caius Gabriel Cibber, according to its listing (Bedfordshire Archives calls it mid nineteenth century); moved to the Long Water in the late nineteenth century

people.name: Anthony Grey, 11th Earl of Kent
people.who: the owner who made the Long Water with his mother Amabel and his wife Mary; father of Henry, Duke of Kent
events: gave the old house a classical north front (about 1671 to 1676)
began a new formal walled garden south of the house
died while playing bowls at Tunbridge Wells

people.name: Amabel Benn, Countess of Kent (the 'Good Countess')
people.who: the second wife of Henry Grey, 10th Earl of Kent, and mother of Anthony, 11th Earl, who ran Wrest for him as a boy and helped make the Long Water
events: married Henry Grey, later 10th Earl of Kent
was widowed and brought up the young 11th Earl
began a new formal garden south of the old house with her son Anthony

people.name: Mary, Countess of Kent and Baroness Lucas of Crudwell
people.who: the heiress wife of Anthony, 11th Earl of Kent, whose inheritance from her father in 1671 helped pay for the old house's north front
events: married Anthony Grey and was made Baroness Lucas of Crudwell
inherited a large estate when her father died
died, a few months after her husband

people.name: Henry Wynne
people.who: the London instrument maker who signed and dated the Wrest sundial plate in 1682 (the listing wrongly calls him an architect)
events: made a sundial for Windsor Castle with the monogram of Charles II

people.name: Thomas Carew
people.who: the Cavalier poet who wrote 'To my friend G.N. from Wrest' while staying at Wrest in 1639
events: wrote 'To my friend G.N. from Wrest' at Wrest
